newsitem.title: IRAQ: Iraq's foreign minister leaves for New York.
newsitem.headline: Iraq's foreign minister leaves for New York.

text.p: Foreign Minister Mohammed Saeed al-Sahaf has left for New York to lobby the U.N. Security Council to lift sanctions on Iraq, the official Iraqi News Agency said on Monday.
"His visit to New York comes within the periodic review of the embargo imposed on Iraq," INA said. It said Sahaf would meet members of the Security Council and U.N. Secretary-General Kofi Annan.
On March 3 the Security Council holds a review, conducted every two months, of the sanctions imposed on Baghdad for its August 1990 invasion of Kuwait.
Terms imposed after Iraqi troops were driven from Kuwait in the 1991 Gulf War require Baghdad to dispose of weapons of mass destruction before the embargo on Iraqi oil exports can be lifted.

But Rolf Ekeus, head of the U.N. Special Commission in charge of destroying Iraq's weapons of mass destruction said in Baghdad on Sunday he was not yet satisfied all banned weapons had been eliminated.
